page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-32xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 4th Generation Intel Xeon 6455B processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores with a sustained clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1024 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 60 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX, and features a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs or local storage drives are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core computational throughput and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier scores in multi-core metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 22175.0, a stress-ng multi-core result of 139186.68, and a PassMark CPU score of 117766.74. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 480.81 GB/sec, while write operations hit 213.95 GB/sec. Application testing shows strong database performance, recording 155.31 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 36342.33 in PassMark database operations, complemented by 115.84 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Without hypervisor overhead or bundled local storage, this bare-metal profile provides direct hardware access suited for high-density enterprise software. Cost efficiency is driven by the high compute frequency paired with 1 TB of DDR5 RAM, allowing organizations running large-footprint licensed software or massive in-memory architectures to consolidate multiple smaller nodes. It is especially suited for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases, real-time analytics, and heavy scientific simulations requiring robust AVX-512 or AMX execution.
